veranderings.voor: Hy deel die hoofstukke wat oorbly in twee helftes.
veranderings.na: Hy verdeel die hoofstukke wat oorbly, in twee helftes.
veranderings.rede: Without a comma the phrase reads as chapters that 'remain in two halves'; 'verdeel' is also the natural verb for splitting something into parts.

veranderings.voor: gaan soek hy self vir meneer Botha
veranderings.na: gaan soek hy self meneer Botha
veranderings.rede: 'Soek vir iemand' copies English 'look for'; standard Afrikaans takes a direct object after 'soek'.

veranderings.voor: of sy antwoord reg is nie
veranderings.na: of sy antwoorde reg is nie
veranderings.rede: There are two questions, so there are two answers and the noun should be plural.

veranderings.voor: Sy wil hulle voor die naweek nasien.
veranderings.na: Sy wil dit voor die naweek nasien.
veranderings.rede: In written Afrikaans 'dit' is the usual pronoun for things such as reports; 'hulle' reads as if it refers to the learners.
'In wees' is spoken classroom shorthand; in the narrative text 'ingehandig word' is clearer, while the dialogue later can keep the spoken form.
